sources.title: Updated biography: former rector and Diplomatic Academy director, education and displacement panel
sources.findings: Read the updated College of Europe biography. It explicitly ends the rector term in December 2025 and the EU Diplomatic Academy directorship in December 2025, the latter starting in August 2022. It supports the Sapienza political-science degree, 2008–2014 Chamber service, 2014–2019 EU offices and January 2020–September 2021 co-chairmanship of the UN internal-displacement panel. Do not retain present-tense leadership from older partner biographies or infer a research doctorate from rector status. Internal displacement is distinct from crossing an international border as a refugee. Peripheral advisory memberships are not all independently refreshed or reproduced.

sources.title: XVII legislature activity record: birth, Chamber resignation and ministerial dates
sources.findings: Read the Senate-hosted printable XVII-legislature record after the historical URL returned a JavaScript challenge. It explicitly says deputy, identifies birth in Rome on 16 June 1973, and dates resignation from the Chamber for incompatibility to 30 October 2014. The ministry record separates Minister of Foreign Affairs, 22 February–28 August, from the expanded Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation title, 29 August–31 October 2014. The host being the Senate does not make her a senator. Distinguish Chamber resignation from ministerial departure and later EU assumption of office.

sources.publisher: Italian Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation
sources.title: Historical minister biography: parliamentary elections and 2013 NATO Parliamentary Assembly delegation role
sources.findings: Read the Italian foreign ministry’s historical biography. It confirms elections in 2008 and 2013 and the 1 August 2013 election as head of Italy’s NATO Parliamentary Assembly delegation. That role is not NATO Secretary General or chair of the entire alliance. The parliamentary defence committee secretary role is not national defence minister. Older party and association descriptions are historical context, not a comprehensive current-office list.

sources.title: 1 November 2014: Mogherini succeeds Catherine Ashton as High Representative and Commission Vice-President
sources.findings: Read EEAS’s archived 1 November 2014 article. It dates actual succession to Catherine Ashton and the combined High Representative, Commission Vice-President and EEAS leadership roles. August appointment and October parliamentary hearing preceded assumption of office. Its 2008 first election overrides a search-visible EPRS summary saying 2009. The quoted aspirations for a common policy are not proof of achieved institutional unity. The exact end date is not taken from an original appointment’s projected October 2019 endpoint; the later handover occurred in December 2019.

sources.title: 14 July 2015: joint statement by Mogherini and Zarif announcing the JCPOA
sources.findings: Read the 14 July 2015 Mogherini–Zarif statement from Vienna announcing the final JCPOA text negotiated with the E3/EU+3. It describes collective negotiations and prospective implementation, not an agreement personally authored or implemented by her alone. Distinguish agreement, later adoption/implementation and later international developments. It concerns nuclear-related sanctions rather than all sanctions on Iran. Claims about future exclusively peaceful activity and lasting security are commitments or expectations, not guarantees of permanent compliance. Linked full agreement, annexes and video were not all inspected.

sources.title: 16 January 2016: joint statement on JCPOA Implementation Day
sources.findings: Read the 16 January 2016 joint statement on Implementation Day. It says the IAEA had verified the relevant commitments for that stage, while the High Representative coordinated the Joint Commission. Diplomatic coordination is not personal technical nuclear inspection. Nuclear-related economic and financial sanctions relief is not universal removal of every sanction, and this historical statement is not a description of the 2026 sanctions regime or a guarantee of later compliance.

sources.title: Rectors of the College of Europe: 1 September 2020–4 December 2025 tenure
sources.findings: Read the current historical rectors list, which gives 1 September 2020–4 December 2025 for Mogherini. It separately lists Ewa Ośniecka-Tamecka from 12 December 2025 through 30 June 2026 and João Gomes Cravinho from 1 July 2026. This supports completed departure and prevents preserving a stale current-rector title. Do not fill the interval between 4 and 12 December with an invented acting appointment. The roster is an office chronology, not a criminal finding.

sources.title: 26 May 2020 appointment announcement, effective 1 September
sources.findings: Read the College’s appointment announcement with a 26 May 2020 press-release link and the explicit future start of 1 September 2020. It identifies the Administrative Council’s appointment on the Academic Council’s proposal and predecessor Jörg Monar. The earlier visiting-professor role is not an earned doctorate or prior rector tenure. The later historical roster confirms the appointment actually took effect. Current footer links to campuses do not prove all campuses existed or operated under the same arrangement in May 2020.

sources.title: 2 December 2025: searches, detentions and scope of suspected procurement offences
sources.findings: Read the EPPO’s 2 December 2025 release. It describes searches authorised by the investigating judge, three detained suspects, and the 2021–2022 tender for EU-funded junior-diplomat training. The alleged advance sharing of tender information and possible offences are investigative suspicions, not established guilt. The release does not name the suspects; her identity is corroborated by the following role-specific release and Reuters. OLAF supported the process; prosecutors, investigating judge and Belgian police have distinct roles. The event was not an arrest during her 2014–2019 EU tenure.

sources.title: 3 December 2025: formal notification of accusations, release and presumption of innocence
sources.findings: Read EPPO’s 3 December 2025 follow-up. The rector, a senior College employee and a senior Commission official had been detained the previous day. After questioning they were formally notified of accusations involving procurement fraud/corruption, conflict of interest and professional secrecy, then released because they were not considered flight risks. Release is not acquittal or discontinuance; formal notification is not conviction, nor proof that a full criminal trial had already begun. The office states the presumption of innocence and withholds further details to protect the investigation.

sources.title: 4 December 2025: rector resignation and lawyer’s denial of wrongdoing
sources.findings: Read Reuters’s 4 December 2025 account of her resignation statement and her lawyer’s denial of wrongdoing and confirmation of cooperation. It links her personally to the procurement investigation, while the college roster corroborates the end of the rector term. Allegations remain attributed and unproven in these records. Another suspect’s retirement plans are not her retirement or a dismissal verdict. The historical photograph caption is not a new 2025 diplomatic office or proof of a 2025 press conference. This report alone does not establish a final 2026 judicial outcome.

sources.title: 3 November 2026 event recap: The EU, NATO and coalitions of the willing
sources.findings: Read Johns Hopkins SAIS Europe’s event recap under the 3 November 2026 event. It records a completed talk and discussion with students, facilitated by Nathalie Tocci, about military threats, democratic resilience, interdependence and European strategic autonomy. This is recent actual personal activity rather than only an invitation or prospective programme. Her views, time horizons for capabilities and suggested coalitions are political analysis, not adopted EU or NATO decisions. No recording was viewed and no separate transcript was inspected.

portraitReview.credit: © European Union / Christophe Licoppe; crop by Sikander
portraitReview.unresolved: Read Commons cropped and parent records. Photograph dated 28 October 2024 at the Bruges academic-year opening; original 4000×2667 group frame uploaded by Sikander on 31 October at 20:12, cropped 358×538 version at 20:24 with a documented 0.76-degree rotation. The parent identifies Federica Mogherini, Herman Van Rompuy, Ursula von der Leyen and Dirk De fauw; the event description focusing on von der Leyen is not itself a visual confirmation of the cropped subject. Author/credit is Christophe Licoppe–European Union, not the crop uploader. Both pages mark CC BY 4.0 but flag external licence review as not completed. Rendered attribution years differ between cached cropped and parent pages (2025/2026); neither changes the 2024 photograph date. The linked original Commission photo page timed out. The Commission copyrights page was readable only as a menu of assignment/licence resources, not item-specific licence confirmation. Original cropped JPEG request on 18 November returned curl 22, HTTP 403 and reported HTTP 000; referenced cached file is absent. Identity, colour, crop correspondence, resolution suitability and original-source licence remain to be checked visually and against the original source.
